places.neighborhood: Tawaramachi, Asakusa, Taito City
places.cuisine: Ramen

noodles.notes: Hand-kneaded (te-momi) to order in small batches, giving irregular crinkles that grip the soup; springy, chewy bite, boiled just firm. A thin straight noodle option is also offered alongside the signature medium-thick hand-kneaded noodle.

ramen.signature_bowl: Shoyu ramen with hand-kneaded medium-thick noodles, topped with ajitama (seasoned egg)
ramen.chashu: Two styles served together: low-temperature-cooked pork loin with a delicate, ham-like texture, and charcoal-grilled (aburi) pork belly for sweet rendered fat and a smoky char aroma.

gf.note: Noodles are wheat-based and the shoyu tare relies on soy sauce; no gluten-free noodle or tare option is documented.

vegan.note: Broth is built on whole chicken stock (with seafood/dried-goods depth) and the shop's signature toppings include pork chashu; no plant-based broth is documented.

ramen.pantheon: A quietly refined Tokyo chicken-shoyu bowl: whole-chicken stock is coaxed into a glassy, semi-transparent amber broth, then finished with a pool of chicken fat and a tare blended from three different soy sauces for layered, restrained umami rather than salt or heft. It sits in the modern Tokyo shoyu lineage — the kind of clear, delicate, technique-driven bowl built to let hand-kneaded wheat noodles and a whole-chicken stock speak for themselves.

noodles.notes: Hand-kneaded (te-momi) in-house from Hokkaido wheat; thick, curly/crimped strands with a chewy, springy bite.

ramen.signature_bowl: 手もみ中華ソバ (Hand-Kneaded Chinese Soba) — the shop's award-recognized bowl, shoyu-tare duck-and-chicken broth with hand-kneaded noodles and duck chashu.
ramen.chashu: Duck breast chashu, seared/grilled (aburi-style) first to render off excess fat before slicing — lean, juicy, and distinct from the usual pork loin/belly.

gf.note: No gluten-free noodle or tare option is documented; the hand-kneaded wheat noodles and shoyu-based tare are standard.

vegan.note: No plant-based broth or chashu-free vegan option is documented; the broth is duck/chicken/niboshi-based throughout.

ramen.pantheon: A modern Tokyo craft-soba bowl built on a five-hour whole-chicken and duck stock layered with a water-extracted niboshi-kombu dashi — the duck's musky richness is tamed by chicken into a clean, additive-free umami rarely found in classic shoyu ramen. It reads as an update of old-school Tokyo chuka soba, swapping pork for poultry and dried-fish depth.

ramen.signature_bowl: 百年醤油らうめん (Hyakunen Shoyu Rauumen / "100-Year Soy Sauce Rauumen")
ramen.chashu: Pork chashu, seasoned then hung and roasted over direct flame in the old-fashioned way, served in generous portion as the bowl's main enrichment.
notable_toppings: slow-rehydrated menma (soaked roughly a week using an old-fashioned method before seasoning)

gf.note: Wheat-based noodles and a soy-sauce (shoyu) tare made with Yamasa soy sauce; no gluten-free noodle or tare option is documented.

vegan.note: Broth is built on chicken stock and the bowl is topped with pork chashu and fish naruto; no plant-based broth option is documented.

ramen.pantheon: This is the bowl where Tokyo shoyu ramen itself began: a 1910 recipe painstakingly rebuilt from historical research into a clean, clear chicken broth laced with soy sauce, the direct ancestor of every clear-soup Tokyo shoyu ramen that followed. Nothing flashy — just old-fashioned menma, hand-roasted chashu, and a bright, savory shoyu backbone that reads as the root of the family tree rather than a modern reinterpretation of it.

ramen.pantheon: Raishuken pours a clear amber shoyu broth simmered slowly from chicken, pork, and vegetables — the gentle, faintly sweet chuka soba that defined Tokyo ramen for decades before tonkotsu and paitan trends arrived. Its firm-bitten pork shoulder chashu and medium curly noodles, served in a Showa-era Asakusa dining room, are a taste of the capital's original noodle-shop lineage.

The kitchen also breaks from the family-style script with its own sizzling iron-pot tantanmen-style aburasoba, where the sesame-pork broth reduces to a thick, clinging sauce around ultra-thick noodles.

half-boiled soy-marinated egg (ajitama) on the egg ramen

gf.note: Standard wheat ramen/tsukemen noodles from outside noodle makers and a wheat-based tare; no gluten-free noodle or menu option is documented.

vegan.note: Broth is pork clear soup blended with seafood stock and finished with chicken-fat aroma oil; no plant-based broth option is documented.

ramen.pantheon: A pork-and-seafood clear soup built in the modern Tokyo shio lineage — gentle and clean on the first sip, then turning saltier and richer as chunky chashu melts its umami into the broth, lifted by a chicken-fat aroma oil. The bowl's real signature isn't a regional style but its meat-forward format: a clear soup engineered to carry an unusually large, rough-cut pile of chashu, with a nod to Kyoto in its kujo-negi option and thick noodle supplier.

notable_toppings: side dish of koji-miso blended with ankimo (monkfish liver) for mid-bowl flavor change

ramen.pantheon: A New-wave miso bowl that fuses two lineages in one pot: Niigata's thick, back-fat-slicked miso richness meets Sapporo's technique of wok-roasting the miso with aromatics before it hits the pork-and-chicken stock. A custom four-miso blend, aged ten days, gives the soup a deep, almost fermented tang, and a side dish of ankimo-spiked miso lets you push the bowl even richer as you eat.

Its calling card isn't tonkotsu but a jet-black tantanmen, where pork-and-chicken broth is married with hot sesame oil, sesame paste, chili oil and vinegar into something creamy and nutty rather than fiery.

ramen.pantheon: This bowl runs on straight fish power: whole "ara" — the heads, bones, and frames of whatever fresh fish came in that day (tai, buri, salmon, conger eel) — are seared over flame and then patiently simmered and skimmed into a clear, golden shio broth, so the soup itself changes character day to day. It sits in Tokyo's contemporary gyokai-shio lineage rather than any old regional style, swapping out pork chashu for delicate shrimp tsumire and chicken-cartilage tsukune that echo the seafood dashi instead of fighting it.

noodles.notes: Custom-milled straight thick wheat noodle (house blend nicknamed "Menu no Hinauta") chosen to let the wheat's own aroma and flavor come through against the delicate broth.

ramen.signature_bowl: Yakiago Shio Ramen (焼きあご塩らー麺) — or the "Tokusei" special version loaded with extra toppings and a triple-chashu plate
ramen.chashu: Two cuts: thin-sliced pork shoulder loin, low-temperature cooked; and a diced, slow-simmered pork belly block — tender, delicate textures that don't fight the clear broth.

gf.note: Standard wheat ramen noodles and a soy-based shio tare; no gluten-free noodle or sauce alternative is documented.

ramen.pantheon: The house speciality is a broth built around yaki-ago — flying fish that's skewered, charcoal-grilled, then sun-dried — an ingredient with deep roots in Kyushu dashi cooking, layered here over a pork-and-chicken base and finished with a fish's own aromatic oil so each sip reads like biting straight into the grilled fish. It's a modern, clear-broth take on shio ramen built to showcase that single smoky, oceanic dashi rather than any one region's classic style.

places.name: うさぎ（神泉のらぁめん屋 うさぎ） (Usagi)
places.neighborhood: Shinsen, Shibuya
places.cuisine: Ramen

noodles.notes: Springy medium-thick noodles built to carry a thick sesame-based sauce for the tantanmen. The house's separate shoyu ramen instead uses fine, silky straight noodles milled from select domestic (Nagano-grown) wheat.

ramen.signature_bowl: Tantanmen, served wet or as shiru-nashi (dry/brothless) — the bowl this shop is known for. A concentrated, sesame-rich sauce built on minced pork is tossed with chewy noodles, with the numbing sansho/flower-pepper tingle (麻) and chili heat (辣) each dialed up separately from mild to fiery. Alongside it, the house also pours a quieter, clear amber shoyu ramen made from a whole-chicken-and-seafood dashi.
ramen.chashu: Thin-sliced pork shoulder (kata-rosu), lightly salted and cooked low-and-slow to a rosy, tender near-rare finish, then quickly seared (aburi-style) for a whisper of char aroma.

gf.note: Wheat noodles and a soy/sesame-based tare and sauce throughout the menu; no gluten-free noodle or tare option is documented.

vegan.note: Broths and sauces are built on chicken, seafood dashi, and minced pork; no plant-based bowl is documented.

ramen.pantheon: A tiny Shibuya back-alley spot that runs two kitchens in one bowl-case: a gentle, clear shoyu ramen simmered from whole chicken and seafood dashi in classic Tokyo style, and — the real draw — a fiery, sesame-creamy tantanmen you can order wet or completely dry (shiru-nashi), tuning your own numbing sansho buzz and chili heat to taste.

places.cuisine: つけ麺

ramen.signature_bowl: Tsukemen (つけめん) — medium-thick wheat noodles served cold alongside a hot, seafood-forward pork-and-chicken dipping sauce; a limited "founding tsukemen" (創業つけめん) recreation of the parent brand's original 2005 recipe also shows up as a seasonal special.
ramen.chashu: Braised pork chashu, sliced thin as a supporting topping rather than the bowl's centerpiece — the dipping sauce, not the pork, is the star. Exact cut/prep not confirmed in sources.

gf.note: Standard wheat tsukemen noodles and shoyu-based dipping sauce; no gluten-free noodle or tare option found.

vegan.note: Dipping sauce is built on seafood dashi plus pork and chicken stock with pork chashu; no plant-based broth option found.

ramen.pantheon: Sharin is the lighter little-sibling brand of Rokurinsha, the Tokyo Station shop credited with popularizing gyokai-tonkotsu (seafood-pork bone) dipping tsukemen in the mid-2000s — this bowl takes that dense double soup and dials it back into an everyday-eatable version, keeping the seafood punch up front while easing off the sheer heft of the original. You taste the lineage in the dipping sauce: fish-stock brightness riding on a pork-and-chicken base, built to be slurped daily rather than as an occasional gut-bomb.

noodles.notes: In-house, ultra-thick, flat-cut wavy noodles with a firm, low-hydration chew and a strong wheat-flour aroma; they're made to be eaten fast before they soften in the broth.

ramen.signature_bowl: Small (regular) Ramen, yasai mashi (extra vegetables) with ninniku (garlic) and abura (pork fat) — the classic Jiro call that shows off the full stack of cabbage, garlic, and fat over the thick noodles and broth.
ramen.chashu: Thick-cut braised pork slices (regular order comes with 2, "chashu" option piles on 4, doubled to 8) soaked and simmered in the shop's own pork broth; the Kabukicho branch's pork is often singled out as leaner and less fatty than at other Jiro locations, making it a gentler entry point to the style while still carrying a big, meaty bite.
notable_toppings: yasai (a mountain of boiled cabbage and bean sprouts)
karame (extra tare for a saltier bowl, by request)

gf.note: Standard wheat-flour noodles and a soy-based tare; no gluten-free noodle or sauce option is documented.

vegan.note: Broth is pork-bone based and every bowl carries pork chashu and pork back-fat; no plant-based broth or protein option is documented.

ramen.pantheon: This bowl is a direct branch of the original Ramen Jiro lineage that essentially invented Tokyo's Jiro-kei cult: a thick, white, emulsified pork-bone broth cut with a punchy shoyu tare and buried under raw garlic, pork back-fat, and a mountain of cabbage and bean sprouts. The Kabukicho shop is known among Jiro regulars as one of the more approachable branches, with broth and chashu that run a shade less fatty than the intensely heavy originals, though it's still built as a late-night, high-calorie fuel stop rather than a delicate soup.

ramen.pantheon: This is the shop that ignited Tokyo's modern niboshi-ramen boom: a thunderously fishy bowl built by simmering 20-plus kinds of dried sardines into a cloudy, fat-slicked pork-and-chicken paitan until the broth tastes like you're chewing whole niboshi. noodles.notes: Custom-order noodles co-developed with Mikawaya Seimen: high-hydration, square-cut thick straight noodles with strong body and a mochi-mochi chew — closer in width to Higashi-Ikebukuro Taishoken than to ultra-thick jiro-style noodles.

ramen.signature_bowl: 濃厚特製つけ麺 (Noukou Tokusei Tsukemen) — the deluxe version of the shop's pioneering rich tonkotsu-gyokai dipping noodles, loaded with extra housemade chashu and a soft ajitama egg.
ramen.chashu: Housemade braised pork chashu, thick-cut; the special (tokusei) bowl doubles the portion. A hearty, meaty counterpoint rather than the headline act — the broth is the star here.

gf.note: Wheat-based custom noodles and a shoyu-leaning animal tare; no gluten-free noodle or broth option is documented.

vegan.note: Broth is built on pork bone, chicken bone, and dried-fish dashi throughout the chain's menu; no plant-based bowl is documented.

ramen.pantheon: Tsujita is widely credited as the pioneer of Tokyo's noukou tonkotsu-gyokai (rich pork-bone-and-seafood) tsukemen — a thick, double-soup dip built from pork bone, chicken bone, dried seafood, kombu, and vegetables into something close to liquid umami concentrate, ladled over springy high-hydration noodles. The house ritual — eat it plain first, then bright with a squeeze of sudachi citrus, then dusted with centuries-old black shichimi pepper — turns one bowl into three distinct tastes before the dip is finished.

noodles.notes: Flat, straight, high-hydration (多加水) noodles supplied by a Shinjuku noodle maker associated with the chan-kei genre; springy and slick with a broad, flat surface that carries extra broth to the mouth, boiled on the softer side.

ramen.signature_bowl: 中華そば (Chuka Soba) — the house classic, a shoyu pork-chintan bowl piled with abundant fresh-sliced chashu; the chashu-loaded もりチャーシュー (dip-style Mori Chashu) is also a popular order.
ramen.chashu: Freshly hand-sliced pork chashu (切り立てチャーシュー) cut from multiple parts of the pig in the same bowl, so pieces range from fatty and sweet to leaner and clean-tasting; served in a generous, overflowing pile rather than a single uniform cut. A spicy chashu (辛味チャーシュー) version is also offered.

gf.note: Straight wheat noodles and a shoyu-based tare; no gluten-free noodle or broth option is documented.

vegan.note: Broth is built on simmered pork bones/pork chashu and every bowl comes topped with pork; no plant-based broth is documented.

ramen.pantheon: A standard-bearer of Tokyo's newer "chan-kei" ramen wave: a bowl brimming to the rim with clear pork chintan broth, its soul a deeply reduced but clean pork essence carried by a bold, dark shoyu tare rather than any heavy fattiness. Flat, slick high-hydration noodles and a mountain of fresh-sliced chashu turn what reads as a simple Tokyo shoyu bowl into an indulgent, chashu-forward feast.

ramen.pantheon: Served as the shime (finishing) bowl inside a sprawling Hokkaido food-hall stall in Shibuya Yokocho, this is a Sapporo-style miso ramen — the archetype that put miso ramen on Japan's map, built around a hearty pork-rich broth and a bold miso tare, with a "rich miso curry ramen" variant on the menu for those who want it turned up further. It reads less as a ramen specialist's bowl and more as the noodle course at the end of a crab, uni, and jingisukan feast.

ramen.pantheon: This bowl traces straight back to Kurume, the town widely credited as tonkotsu ramen's birthplace, and it plays that lineage two ways: a clean, "jun-mi" pork-bone soup that lets the boiled-head-bone broth speak for itself, and a heavier "koku-mi" version loaded with back fat, house miso, and burnt garlic-onion oil for a deeper, muskier hit. The soul of the Shinjuku shop, though, is its Tokyo-only tsukemen — a concentrated tonkotsu-shoyu dip stacked with seared pork offal and finished, izakaya-style, with a rice-porridge chaser instead of the usual soup dilution.

It's finished with a three-stage fried-garlic oil and, on request, a housemade spicy miso, with sibling bowls layering in seafood dashi or an aged soy-sauce-and-backfat riff for those who want more punch.

The result is a lush, orange-tinted shrimp broth — a distinctly Hokkaido specialty rarely found built this way anywhere else.

places.name: 鯛担麺専門店 恋し鯛 (Koishitai (Tai-Tantanmen Specialty Shop))
places.cuisine: French-influenced ramen specializing in tai

noodles.notes: Custom-developed curly (chijire) noodles built to cling to the thick sesame-tai broth; exact thickness shifts by menu item (some versions run thicker), and hydration is not documented.

ramen.signature_bowl: 鯛担麺 (Tai Tantanmen) — Uwajima sea-bream and chicken paitan thickened with an original sesame sauce, topped with rare pork chashu, chicken confit, and spicy meat sauce, finished with a balsamic vinegar drizzle; spice level adjustable to taste.
ramen.chashu: Low-temperature-cooked pork loin chashu served rare (blush-pink center, French sous-vide technique) alongside a soft, moist chicken confit — a French-kitchen take rather than a traditional simmered slab.

gf.note: Wheat-based curly noodles and a sesame/soy-leaning tare; no gluten-free noodle or tare swap is documented.

vegan.note: Broth is built on sea bream and chicken stock with meat-based chashu and confit throughout; no plant-based bowl is documented.

ramen.pantheon: A French-trained chef's love letter to ramen: Uwajima sea bream is simmered into a thick, creamy paitan and married with chicken white broth and a house sesame sauce, then finished tantanmen-style with a drizzle of balsamic vinegar for a savory-sweet top note you won't find anywhere else in the genre.

places.name: らーめん 穀雨 (Ramen Kokū)
places.neighborhood: 桜丘町 (Sakuragaoka-cho), Shibuya
places.cuisine: Ramen

noodles.notes: Custom order noodles from a Tokyo noodle maker (Taiei Shokuhin): medium-thin, wavy, medium hydration, with a firm bite yet smooth, supple throat-feel.

ramen.signature_bowl: Shoyu Wantan-men — clear pork-chicken-seafood broth with plump ginger-scented wontons (choice of 3 or 5) and two styles of honey-roasted chashu; the shio version is equally well-regarded.
ramen.chashu: Roasted, not braised: two cuts served together — leg (momo) hung and roasted plain, and shoulder-loin (kata-rosu) coated in honey and oven-roasted — giving a drier, more fragrant yakibuta character than the usual simmered chashu.
notable_toppings: housemade-style ginger-scented pork wontons (3 or 5 per bowl)
optional table-side crispy fried scallion (age-negi) and housemade garlic chili oil

gf.note: Wheat noodles from an outside noodle maker, wheat-based shoyu tare, and wheat wonton wrappers — no gluten-free option is documented.

vegan.note: Broth is built on pork and chicken bones with bonito/kombu/shiitake dashi, and every noodle dish comes with meat-based chashu and/or pork wontons — no plant-based bowl is documented.

ramen.pantheon: This bowl carries the old-school Tokyo wonton-noodle bloodline of the legendary Tantan-tei, passed down through Meguro's Kazu-ya — a clear pork-and-chicken stock laced with dried bonito, kelp and shiitake that tastes light on first sip but unfolds into a deep, drinkable koku. It's classic shitamachi-style chuka soba, built around silky hand-folded wontons and honey-roasted (not braised) chashu rather than any modern richness arms race.

noodles.notes: Described as firm thin noodles in the spicy shoyu ramen; the shop's tanmen instead uses curled medium noodles (~150g). No evidence noodles are handmade in-house — likely a standard delivered noodle typical of town Chinese restaurants.

ramen.signature_bowl: 達磨辛子ラーメン (Daruma Spicy Ramen) — a spicy shoyu ramen that looks fierier than it tastes, built on a flavorful clear broth with firm thin noodles; the shop's shio-based tanmen (loaded with over five stir-fried vegetables and meat) is an equally popular order.

gf.note: Standard wheat kansui noodles and shoyu/shio tare; no gluten-free noodle or tare option is documented.

vegan.note: Broths are chicken/animal-based and toppings include pork; no plant-based bowl is documented.

ramen.pantheon: A forty-plus-year Shinjuku machi-chuka standby that still cooks ramen the old Tokyo way: light, clear chicken-and-vegetable broth, wok-charred stir-fried vegetables piled over curly noodles for the tanmen, and a shoyu ramen spiked with chili that carries the shop's own name. It is comfort-food Tokyo shoyu rather than a boutique bowl — the kind of everyday ramen a neighborhood has relied on for decades.

ramen.signature_bowl: 鶏白湯SOBA (chicken-paitan soba), ¥2,000 in October 2026; a fresh-truffle shoyu version is ¥3,000.
ramen.chashu: Tender chashu on the standard bowl; reviewers describe it as unremarkable next to the soup.
notable_toppings: a row of seasonal vegetables (pumpkin, lotus root, bell pepper, daikon, sweet potato…)
fried onion and ginger on the side

gf.note: Wheat ramen noodles; no gluten-free option documented.

vegan.note: Chicken-paitan soup throughout.

ramen.pantheon: A Ginza-style take on tori paitan: the chicken soup is pushed to a thick, potage-like cream, then dressed like a small kaiseki plate with a row of seasonal vegetables. Fried onion and ginger on the side let you cut the richness halfway.

richness: Quite rich and creamy, reminiscent of a chicken potage, thick and packed with chicken umami.
oiliness: https://tabelog.com/en/tokyo/A1301/A130101/13230021/dtlrvwlst/B535891550/
Creamy and smooth; easy to finish without tiring of it.
clarity: A thick, creamy paitan — the opposite of a clear soup.
tare_strength: Not described in any source read; scored at the midpoint.

places.name: 九州じゃんがら 銀座店 (Kyushu Jangara Ginza)
places.neighborhood: Ginza 6-chōme (Ginza Katagiri Bldg 1F) — 3 min from Higashi-Ginza (Hibiya line) and from Ginza (Ginza line)
places.cuisine: Kyushu-style tonkotsu ramen (Kyushu Jangara chain) · vegan shoyu ramen

noodles.notes: Thin noodles for the tonkotsu bowls: several wheat flours bound with egg white, cooked to a firm, springy bite; refills (替玉) available.

ramen.signature_bowl: 九州じゃんがら — the mild tonkotsu house bowl; regulars order it 全部入り (everything in).
ramen.chashu: The signature pork is 角肉 — pork belly braised long and de-fatted, from a Nagasaki shippoku recipe — offered as a topping and in the zenbu-iri bowl.
notable_toppings: free pickled mustard greens (takana) and red ginger at the table

gf.note: Wheat-and-egg-white noodles; no gluten-free noodle on the menu.

vegan.note: One plant-based shoyu ramen at Ginza (五葷抜き on request); everything else is pork-bone soup.

ramen.pantheon: Tokyo's own take on Kyushu tonkotsu since 1984. The house bowl softens a pork-bone soul with chicken frames and vegetables into a mild, light soup, while the menu walks the Kyushu map — Bonshan for creamy Kurume/Hakata, Kobonshan for Kumamoto's black-garlic oil. Thin, firm egg-white noodles and the 'zenbu-iri' toppings (braised pork belly, mentaiko, a whole seasoned egg) are the house signature.

richness: 「豚骨、鶏ガラ、数種類の野菜をバランスよく配分し、丁寧に煮出したマイルドな豚骨スープ」 — a pork-bone soup, but billed mild.
oiliness: https://kyushujangara.co.jp/menu/
「軽やかな口当たりが特徴」; the black-garlic oil belongs to Kobonshan, not the house bowl.
clarity: A simmered pork-bone and chicken-frame soup; its sibling Bonshan is billed クリーミー.
tare_strength: A May 2026 diner tasted a burnt-soy-sauce note in the tonkotsu broth.
noodle_firmness: https://kyushujangara.co.jp/menu/
「こりこり感を持った一定の硬さ」「コシのある麺」; one 2026 diner found even barikata a little soft (https://tabelog.com/en/tokyo/A1301/A130101/13000570/dtlrvwlst/B529301857/).
aroma_punch: https://kyushujangara.co.jp/menu/
No aromatic oil on the house bowl; garlic/mayu is Kobonshan's, spice is Karabon's.

noodles.notes: Medium-thick straight noodles that soak up the soup (miso chashu, 2023).

ramen.signature_bowl: みそチャーシュー (miso chashu) — a gentle miso soup over wok-fried bean sprouts, cabbage and pork belly, with four thick slices of pork shoulder; ¥1,300 in 2023.
ramen.chashu: Thick-cut pork shoulder loin (豚肩ロース), tender and fairly lean; four slices on the miso chashu.

gf.note: Wheat ramen noodles; no gluten-free option in any source.

vegan.note: One soup of chicken feet, pig's trotters and vegetables underlies every noodle dish.

ramen.pantheon: A Shōwa machi-chūka bowl with a chain pedigree: the noodle menu's base flavour descends from the 1970s つけ麺大王 that the shop began as, and the miso chashu is built the wok way — bean sprouts, cabbage and pork belly fired over high heat, then soup and a mildly spicy house miso tare added in the pan. It drinks as gently as miso soup; four thick slices of shoulder chashu carry the weight.

richness: 「味噌汁のようなほっこりやさしい、あっさりとしたスープ」
oiliness: https://san-tatsu.jp/articles/272176/

clarity: Miso-seasoned soup likened to miso soup (味噌汁のような) — not a clear broth.
tare_strength: 「決してしょっぱすぎるわけではないのだが、全体的にあっさりとした味わい」
noodle_firmness: https://san-tatsu.jp/articles/272176/
「中太麺はもっちもち」, straight noodles that 「グングンスープを吸い上げていく」 — soft-chewy, not firm.
aroma_punch: https://san-tatsu.jp/articles/272176/
「自家製の味噌だれは少し辛味がある」 — a little heat; no garlic or other aromatic oil mentioned.

places.name: 利尻昆布ラーメン くろおび (Rishiri Kombu Ramen Kuroobi)
places.neighborhood: Roppongi 4-12-5, 六本木144ビル 1F — 2 min from Roppongi Stn exit 7 (Oedo / Hibiya lines)
places.cuisine: Ramen on a broth of additive-free Rishiri kombu (2026 reviews) · Kuroobi Ramen, shio ¥1,300 (October 2026), with belly and loin chashu, shrimp wontons, seasoned egg, menma, green onion and red chili threads; also as a shoyu bowl with a clear amber broth · shrimp wonton ramen; chashu ramen; kombu-water tsukemen with shiso; a winter-limited spicy bowl, "Kagutsuchi"; chilled ramen · shiso gyoza and a value set with gyoza · Ubushuna tea, also sold in the shop; beer and sake

noodles.notes: "The noodles are thin and straight, with a smooth texture" (October 2026); the tsukemen noodles are long and smooth (September 2026).

ramen.signature_bowl: Kuroobi Ramen, shio — ¥1,300 in October 2026, with belly and loin chashu, shrimp wontons, seasoned egg, menma, green onion and red chili threads.
ramen.chashu: Two kinds, belly and loin: "The belly is juicy and tender, while the loin has a firm, meaty texture" (October 2026); thick chashu on the chashu ramen (October 2026).

gf.note: Wheat noodles.

vegan.note: Kombu broth with animal-based ingredients; pork chashu, shrimp wontons.

ramen.pantheon: A clear, additive-free Rishiri-kombu broth, balanced with animal-based stock, over thin straight noodles with two chashu and shrimp wontons.

richness: "a light yet umami-rich broth" (October 2026); "it had a very gentle flavor" (https://tabelog.com/en/tokyo/A1307/A130701/13311548/dtlrvwlst/B537242527/, October 2026).
oiliness: https://tabelog.com/en/tokyo/A1307/A130701/13311548/dtlrvwlst/B536605601/
Shoyu bowl: "The oil floating on the surface added just the right amount of richness… It wasn’t overly greasy" (October 2026).
clarity: "The soup is clear and flavorful" (October 2026); "The broth was beautifully clear" (https://tabelog.com/en/tokyo/A1307/A130701/13311548/dtlrvwlst/B537242527/, October 2026); "The clear amber broth" of the shoyu bowl (https://tabelog.com/en/tokyo/A1307/A130701/13311548/dtlrvwlst/B536605601/).
tare_strength: "The broth had a nice salty taste" (October 2026); shoyu: "the savory aroma of soy sauce came through without being too sharp" (https://tabelog.com/en/tokyo/A1307/A130701/13311548/dtlrvwlst/B536605601/).
noodle_firmness: https://tabelog.com/en/tokyo/A1307/A130701/13311548/dtlrvwlst/B537584936/
"Personally, I found the noodles to be quite prominent" (October 2026); "a smooth texture… a generous portion" (https://tabelog.com/en/tokyo/A1307/A130701/13311548/dtlrvwlst/B536841610/).
aroma_punch: https://tabelog.com/en/tokyo/A1307/A130701/13311548/dtlrvwlst/B537242527/

"It was a bit disappointing that the kombu flavor didn’t stand out more" (October 2026); "the refined flavor of the kombu… lacked a bit of power" (https://tabelog.com/en/tokyo/A1307/A130701/13311548/dtlrvwlst/B537584936/).

places.address_ja: 東京都港区六本木4-4-6 谷口ビル 1F

places.name: R2 SUPPER CLUB

places.cuisine: A lounge bar and restaurant with a DJ (2026 reviews) · cocktails, especially the well-known yuzu mojito; martinis, gin and tonic, whisky sodas; about 50 drinks on the party menus (Tabelog) · food: Cobb salad, crab pasta (May 2026), a seasonal "Vegetarian Plate" and low-carb à la carte dishes (Tabelog shop text) · party courses with two hours of drinks ¥6,600 (20 or more) and a basement course ¥5,500 (Tabelog) · birthday plates and towers
places.address_ja: 東京都港区六本木7-14-23 ラウンドクロス六本木 1F

places.name: 焼鶏 輪 (Yakitori Rin)
places.neighborhood: Roppongi 4-5-14, アーバンビル 1F, down the street beside HUB Roppongi — 2 min from Roppongi Stn exit 7 (Oedo line), 4 min from exit 6 (Hibiya line)

places.address_ja: 東京都港区六本木4-5-14 アーバンビル 1F

places.name: SPIGOLA
places.neighborhood: Roppongi 4-4-4, メゾン六本木 1F, a narrow alley in Roppongi 4-chome — 1 min from Roppongi Stn exit 7 (Oedo line), 3 min from exit 4a (Hibiya line)
places.cuisine: Seasonal Italian (2024–2026 reviews) · lunch with salad (shaved cheese, greens, vegetable jelly), Sayama black tea and dessert such as tiramisu: daily pasta ¥1,800 (porcini and mushroom oil, sea-bream puttanesca, squid ink, smoked salmon in light tomato); Genovese ¥2,200 made with a pesto said to have won a world championship; karasumi pasta; carbonara (2025–2026 reviews) · dinner omakase about ¥12,000 (Tabelog): in June 2026, panzanella with vegetables from Yatsugatake, burrata and peach, chilled corn soup, porcini cutlet, handmade pasta with charcoal-grilled sweetfish and uruka, beef; homemade wild-boar prosciutto and karasumi shortbread (October 2025); bottarga pasta (June 2025) · wine by the glass, chosen by sommelier Miura (August 2024 visit); a duck-themed dinner event (January 2026)
places.address_ja: 東京都港区六本木4-4-4 メゾン六本木 1F

places.name: たいやき わかば (Taiyaki Wakaba)
places.neighborhood: Wakaba 1-10, 小沢ビル 1F — from Yotsuya-mitsuke toward Shinjuku, the second lane on the left, fourth shop on the right; 4–5 min from Yotsuya Stn
places.cuisine: Taiyaki shop since 1953 (official site) · taiyaki ¥250 each: a thin, crisp shell less than a millimetre thick, house tsubu-an packed from head to tail, salty-sweet in the old Edo way, each fish baked one at a time in the shop's own irons with "わかば" on the tail (official site; 2026 reviews) · house anko to take home: 300 g ¥600, 600 g ¥1,200, 1 kg ¥1,950 (official site) · April–October: mitarashi or an-dango ¥180 a stick; July–September: kakigori ¥500–800, shiratama azuki ¥500 (official site) · free self-service tea when eating in (October 2026)
places.address_ja: 東京都新宿区若葉1-10 小沢ビル 1F

places.name: ラ・ボーテ (La Beaute)
places.neighborhood: Yotsuya 2-3-19, 四谷大新ビル 2F, in a back lane — 3 min from Exit 2 of Yotsuya Stn (Namboku Line), 5 min from JR (Yotsuya exit)
places.cuisine: Herbal (yakuzen) hot pots with an Italian touch and at least 12 kinds of vegetables, often 20 or more (Tabelog; 2025–26 reviews) · dinner hot pot sets with appetizers and dessert: the "Anti-Aging Nabe" with a tomato-and-herb broth and a basil-and-herb broth, finished as cheese risotto; a beauty hot pot of soft-shell turtle salt broth and spicy chicken-bone broth; a detox hot pot in curry and salt; choose chicken, beef, pork or fish; meatballs with Job's tears (2025–26 reviews) · appetizers such as pâté, spring rolls, chickpea croquettes, eggplant tartare; herbal sake and herbal beer · lunch: two herbal soups (e.g. pumpkin clam chowder, burdock) with salad and 14-grain rice, ¥900–1,000; teriyaki pork ¥1,200; rice size free (2025) · the owner's own ice creams, from a stock of over 300 recipes, e.g. red wine and fig, brown-sugar coconut (2025–26 reviews)
places.address_ja: 東京都新宿区四谷2-3-19 四谷大新ビル 2F

places.name: 北島亭 (Kitajima Tei)
places.neighborhood: Yotsuya Sanei-cho 15-2, JHCビル 1F, under a yellow awning — 5–7 min from Yotsuya Stn
places.cuisine: Hearty classic French in generous portions (Tabelog; 2026 reviews) · two courses, ¥16,940 (three dishes) and ¥18,150 (four, adding fish), unchanged in price for 12 years per an August 2026 regular: amuses (chilled cucumber soup with mint, bacon quiche, légumes à la grecque), a cold starter from about six (the signature Nemuro uni on cauliflower cream under consommé jelly with junsai; a charlotte of red snow crab wrapped in asparagus; marinated spiny lobster +¥1,210), a hot starter (Hungarian foie gras with corn galette +¥1,210; cèpes Bordelaise; stuffed red pepper with mozzarella and shellfish), fish (Choshi flounder in a potato crust with soupe de poissons sauce), meat from three (Ibaraki wagyu rump with shallot butter, Zao duck with Madeira, Kawamata shamo chicken, lamb), granité, dessert (black-tea pudding with caramel ice cream, Kyoho grape tart), six petits fours · wine pairing, e.g. five glasses ¥10,285 (August 2026); totals about ¥23,000–30,000 a head
places.address_ja: 東京都新宿区四谷三栄町15-2 JHCビル 1F

places.name: 栄進館 (Eishinkan)
places.neighborhood: Yotsuya Saka-machi 1-8, at the entrance of the Eishinkan inn on the corner by the Yotsuya 1-chome crossing — 5 min from Yotsuya Stn
places.cuisine: Small bakery in the entrance of a long-running inn, sharing the bread served at the inn's breakfast (September 2026) · kinako butter bread ¥260 (mini ¥150): organic kinako and Hokkaido cream butter wrapped in rice-flour dough, crunchy outside and molten inside, on sale since January 2021 (2026 reviews) · daily breads such as maple sugar butter, crunchy sugar butter, milk butter ¥250, green-onion salt chicken with lotus root ¥290, egg mayo ¥200, sesame sausage, apple cinnamon, raisin nuts, kinako croissant, strawberry chocolate, almond chocolate Danish, a pizza of the week (2025–26 reviews) · free drink with purchase
places.address_ja: 東京都新宿区四谷坂町1-8

places.name: 博多豚骨らぁ麺一絆 上野御徒町本店 (Hakata Tonkotsu Ramen Ichiban)
places.neighborhood: Ueno 6-chōme, deep in Ameyoko — 1 min from JR Okachimachi North Exit
places.cuisine: Hakata tonkotsu ramen, billed as the birthplace of "clear tonkotsu" — a pork-bone broth without the usual cloudiness (Tabelog) · menu (Tabelog, October 2026): plain tonkotsu ramen ¥650, tonkotsu ramen ¥800, special ¥1,000, tonkotsu vegetable ramen ¥1,000, clear tonkotsu vegetable ramen ¥1,200, special clear tonkotsu ramen ¥1,650 (rare chashu around the bowl, three toppings) · extra noodles, vegetables, rice ¥150 each; chashu or chicken-salt rice bowl ¥400; tamago kake gohan ¥350; rare chashu ¥300 · stir-fried vegetables in a thick sauce served on a separate plate; free mentaiko on the table
places.address_ja: 東京都台東区上野6-4-18

places.name: カフェ ベル (Cafe Bell)
places.neighborhood: Ueno Park, International Library of Children's Literature 1F — about 15 min on foot from JR Uguisudani or through the park from JR Ueno
places.cuisine: Library café and lunch counter (Tabelog; reviews) · curry rice ¥550 (November 2025); large omurice curry with salad, soup ¥100 (July 2026); hamburg curry; Napolitan spaghetti, known as the house speciality (November 2025) · value set ¥700: fried white fish with pink tartar sauce and twice-cooked pork in a bento box (July 2026); daily special ¥800 (August 2026); pasta, sandwiches, bento · coffee ¥400, iced ¥450 (up from ¥300/¥320 early 2026); drinks ¥150 with lunch · cake set ¥650 (October 2026); shaved ice with unlimited syrup, soft-serve
places.address_ja: 東京都台東区上野公園12-49 国際子ども図書館内 1F

places.name: らぁめん千寿 御徒町店 (ramen senju)
places.neighborhood: Ueno 4-chōme, 美濃里ビル 1F — 1 min from JR Okachimachi North Exit and Exit A5 of Ueno-Hirokoji / Ueno-Okachimachi Stns
places.cuisine: Sapporo miso ramen: the first Tokyo shop of ramen senju, founded in Sapporo in 2002 (Tabelog Hokkaido ramen 100 in 2024 and 2025); a rich miso soup stir-fried from over 30 ingredients, with curly medium-thick noodles made for the shop by Ichinobu Seimen, as the listing romanizes it (Tabelog) · menu (Tabelog, August 2026): miso ramen ¥1,100, with bean sprouts and ginger ¥1,250, chashu ¥1,500, special ¥1,600; the same four in salt and soy sauce · table seasonings: pepper, garlic, chilli oil, niboshi vinegar
places.address_ja: 東京都台東区上野4-2-5 美濃里ビル 1F

places.name: sardexka
places.neighborhood: Shitaya 1-chōme, 竹内マンション 1F, on a quiet street between Uguisudani and Iriya — 5 min from JR Uguisudani South Exit or Iriya Stn
places.cuisine: Spanish and Basque cooking with seasonal Japanese ingredients ("sardexka" is Basque for fork, per the website); Tabelog Spanish 100 in 2024 and 2026 · dinner (Tabelog, January 2026): omakase of about 10 small dishes ¥9,000 or about 9 dishes ¥7,000; desserts and a closing dish extra · lunch courses ¥7,700, or ¥8,800 with dessert (August 2026); paella course ¥8,800 (November 2026) · dishes reviewers name: watermelon gazpacho, piquillo peppers, pisto, octopus with potatoes or beans, stuffed peppers, crisp sea bream, Hokkaido salmon, eggplant and pork-blood spring rolls, seafood paella, coffee blancmange · wine
places.address_ja: 東京都台東区下谷1-6-7 竹内マンション 1F

places.cuisine: Neighbourhood soba with rice-bowl sets and an evening izakaya menu (2026 reviews) · lunch sets of soba with a rice bowl and salad ¥800 (July–August 2026) — katsudon, gyudon, egg bowl, inari (March–May 2026) · mori soba set with inari ¥800 (May 2026) · tamago-toji soba ¥800 (March 2026) · curry nanban soba ¥850, kake soba ¥450 (September 2026) · chilled tanuki soba (June 2026) · cold noodles ¥700 (August 2026) · weekly specials (2023, 2026) · also ramen and yakisoba (June 2026) · evening: drinks with two dishes ¥1,500 (September 2026)
places.address_ja: 東京都中央区日本橋人形町1-2-9

places.name: 来福亭 (Raifuku Tei)
places.neighborhood: Nihonbashi-Ningyocho 1-17-10, an old house between 玉ひで and an old coffee shop (August 2026) — 1 min from Ningyocho Stn exit A1, 5 min from Suitengumae Stn exit A8
places.cuisine: Old Tokyo yoshoku (2026 reviews) · omurice ¥850 (October 2026); omurice with a small menchi katsu ¥1,200, the favourite (August–October 2026); mini omurice with hayashi sauce (September 2026) · menchi katsu rice ¥1,100 (August 2026) · katsudon with miso soup and pickles ¥1,200 (June 2026) · pork sauté ¥1,100, crab fried rice ¥850 (June 2026) · chicken rice ¥750, ham salad ¥700 (August 2026) · curry; hamburg steak, ham rice, fried scallops (2026) · beer: small bottle ¥400, medium ¥650 (2026)
places.address_ja: 東京都中央区日本橋人形町1-17-10

places.name: わかい (Wakai)
places.neighborhood: Nihonbashi-Horidomecho 1-7-16, a narrow back alley, red noren and brick tiles — 3 min from Ningyocho Stn, 6 min from Kodenmacho Stn
places.cuisine: Old-school Sapporo-style miso ramen: bean sprouts and minced pork stir-fried in a wok, then simmered with a pork-bone broth and white-miso seasoning; medium-thick curly yellow egg noodles (2026 reviews) · miso ramen ¥900 (Tabelog menu, January 2026; ¥950 in one August 2026 review) · shoyu and shio ramen; salt butter ramen (2026) · toppings: kuki-wakame seaweed stems ¥100, chashu ¥150–¥200, corn ¥100, butter ¥50, menma (2025–26); miso butter corn ¥1,050 (October 2026) · mini fried rice ¥200, often sold out (2026) · rice · pepper, shichimi, chili oil and grated garlic on the table
places.address_ja: 東京都中央区日本橋堀留町1-7-16

places.name: 天ぷら やぐち (Tempura Yaguchi)
places.neighborhood: Nihonbashi-Ningyocho 2-9-7, 大江戸アクセス2 1F, on Daimon-dori — 5 min from Ningyocho Stn exit A3 or Suitengumae Stn exit 7
places.cuisine: Edo-style tempura omakase in the Mikawa Zezankyo tradition, about 17–20 pieces at lunch or dinner (2025–26 reviews) · a 2026 course: turnip with snow-crab sauce, two shrimp and the shrimp heads, sumi-ika and aori-ika, Kumamoto red eggplant, megochi, Kashima clams, fugu milt with truffle salt, oysters, sea urchin wrapped in shiso, anago, ending with a mini kakiage tendon or tencha (February–July 2026) · seasonal: young ayu, mountain vegetables, matsutake, ginkgo (2025–26) · beer, sake and wine · reviewers spent ¥20,000–¥50,000 a head (2025–26)
places.address_ja: 東京都中央区日本橋人形町2-9-7 大江戸アクセス2 1F

places.name: はし本 (Hashimoto)
places.neighborhood: Roppongi 4-4-11, 第1六本木ヴィレッジビル 1F, a quiet street by Tokyo Midtown — 2 min from Roppongi Stn exit 7 (Oedo line)
places.cuisine: An izakaya built around duck hot pot, served since the shop opened (October 2026), with homemade drinking dishes and sake (Tabelog shop text) · duck hot-pot course with three appetizers, the hot pot and zosui to finish ¥4,750 (Tabelog) · the hot pot: duck and garlic chives, chicken tsukune, napa cabbage and green onion in a slightly rich soy broth (November 2025) · à la carte in small portions sized to the group: deep-fried yam with nori, smoked daikon with mascarpone, agedashi tofu, water octopus, tonkatsu, tempura (2025–2026 reviews) · about 15 sakes such as Sharaku, Mimuro Sugi, Yuki no Bosha, Houou Bidan, Nanbu Bijin; seasonal fruit liqueurs; shochu, whisky, wine (November 2025–January 2026) · about ¥5,000–7,000 a head (2025–2026 reviews)
places.address_ja: 東京都港区六本木4-4-11 第1六本木ヴィレッジビル 1F

places.name: 旬菜魚 藍 (Shunsai Gyo Ai)
places.neighborhood: Roppongi 4-4-3, 六本木協和ビル西館 1F, a side street next to Tokyo Midtown — 1 min from Roppongi Stn exit 7 (Oedo line), 4 min (Hibiya line)
places.cuisine: Seafood-led Japanese kaiseki and kappo (2022–2025 reviews) · speciality ingredients (Tabelog shop text): sliced 500 g black abalone from Maizuru, Kitamurasaki sea urchin from Rishiri prepared without alum, hairy crab · soft-shelled turtle course ¥19,700, the hot pot made with junmai sake, kombu and a splash of light soy (Tabelog) · in reviews: glutinous rice topped with homemade karasumi; seasonal hassun; Kōbako crab with crab vinegar (November 2023, November 2025); aged fugu and Seki mackerel sashimi; Maizuru oysters, salt-water uni, hamo sashimi and grilled hamo, grilled wild eel (September 2025); horse sashimi, narwhal bacon, moon-bear hot pot (October–November 2025); tempura such as cod shirako and Brussels sprouts; sea-bream rice to finish · sake and shochu including rare bottles · reviewers paid about ¥15,000–20,000, up to ¥50,000+ with a host's choices
places.address_ja: 東京都港区六本木4-4-3 六本木協和ビル西館 1F

places.name: Bistro Vino
places.neighborhood: Roppongi 6-6-9, ピラミデビル 1F, behind Motoazabu Police Station towards Roppongi Hills — 2 min from Roppongi Stn
places.cuisine: A casual wine bistro: Western lunches, then wine and grilled dishes at night (2026 reviews) · lunch: cheese-avocado burger with fries and salad ¥1,880, chicken steak ¥1,480, pork sauté set with rice or bread; a ¥3,000 course with meat, salad and soup (July 2026) · night: over 100 bottled wines from around the world (September 2026); tapas platter; burrata or mozzarella with seasonal fruit and prosciutto; oysters; mini truffle hash browns with Pecorino; gnocchi in Gorgonzola cream; liver pâté; grilled meats, pasta, shrimp and mushrooms in basil butter; tiramisu (2025–2026 reviews) · Thanksgiving dinner with turkey ¥8,980, 21–29 November 2026 (Tabelog) · glass wine ¥1,000–1,400, highball ¥880 (July 2026)
places.address_ja: 東京都港区六本木6-6-9 ピラミデビル 1F

places.name: たか野 (Takano)
places.neighborhood: Roppongi 4-4-3, 六本木協和ビル西館 1F, at the end of a one-way street behind Tokyo Midtown — about 3 min from Roppongi Stn
places.cuisine: Obanzai and seasonal kappo shaped by training in Osaka and Kyoto, with traditional Niigata dishes (Tabelog shop text) · obanzai lined up on the counter, such as herring with eggplant (nishin nasu), nikogori, iidako, nikujaga, mozuku vinegar; a monthly-changing à la carte and an omakase (2023–2025 reviews) · winter fugu — sashimi, fried, shirako with salt, fin sake; Kōbako crab; matsutake; hamo in summer; bamboo-shoot tempura in spring · to finish: sea-bream chazuke with sesame ground in front of you, sea-bream rice made into onigiri, fugu zosui simmered for hours at weekends · sake from Niigata such as Tsurunoe Yukionna; barley shochu · about ¥8,000–15,000 a head (2024–2026 reviews)
places.address_ja: 東京都港区六本木4-4-3 六本木協和ビル西館 1F

places.name: 中華そば 山下 (Chuka Soba Yamashita)
places.neighborhood: Yotsuya 2-3-6, パルム四谷 1F, on Shinjuku-dōri — 5–6 min from Yotsuya Stn, 7 min from Yotsuya-sanchome
places.cuisine: Lunch-only niboshi ramen shop (2026 reviews) · niboshi chuka soba ¥800, a clear broth of four kinds of niboshi, kombu and shiitake, light but rich in niboshi flavour (July–October 2026); seasoned-egg version ¥950 · rich niboshi soba ¥1,000 (special ¥1,350), a thick chicken-and-pork paitan with niboshi (May–June 2026) · straight medium-thick noodles; chashu of several kinds; free rich lemon and fish powder to add (April 2026) · zosui rice for the last of the soup; chashu rice bowl · seasonal limited bowls, e.g. a Yen Sanjo-style special (April 2026) · free barley tea in a beer mug; highballs at lunch
places.address_ja: 東京都新宿区四谷2-3-6 パルム四谷 1F

places.name: 酒肴 味 (Shukou Aji)
places.neighborhood: Sanei-cho 3-6, down a small alley — 5–6 min from Yotsuya Stn
places.cuisine: Fish izakaya with a handwritten daily menu of fish bought at Toyosu (2024–26 reviews) · appetizer trio ¥500, e.g. simmered oysters, shallots with miso, whitebait, simmered whelk · sashimi platters (kinmedai, kohada and akagai, katsuo, hamo, seared Matsukawa flounder), the signature "moon-viewing" sardines with egg yolk and green onion, aji namero (about ¥800), ankimo ¥850, simmered anago and kinmedai, grilled fish roe, tempura of firefly squid or vegetables, fried young ayu, tamagoyaki sweet or savoury, okara, "yude pon" fish balls served since opening, oki-jiru fish soup ¥1,000 (2024–26 reviews) · sake such as Ichinokura hot ¥700, shochu, Sapporo Lager Akaboshi
places.address_ja: 東京都新宿区三栄町3-6

places.neighborhood: Yotsuya 2-9-15, サンサーラ四谷ビル B1F, down the stairs just off Shinjuku-dōri — 7 min from Yotsuya Stn, 10 min from Yotsuya-sanchome; Spice Curry Shokudo is on the ground floor

places.address_ja: 東京都新宿区四谷2-9-15 サンサーラ四谷ビル B1F

places.name: スパイスカレー食堂 四谷本店 (Spice Curry Shokudo Yotsuya Honten)
places.neighborhood: Yotsuya 2-9-15, サンサーラ四谷 1F — 5 min from Yotsuya Stn (take the slope to the left of the ticket gate), 7 min from Yotsuya-sanchome; Love Asia is in the basement
places.cuisine: Sri Lankan rice-and-curry plates (2026 reviews) · black chicken curry ¥1,300, the classic, fairly spicy: jasmine rice with shredded chicken curry, parippu (coconut lentil curry), green bean and potato curry, purple-cabbage pickle, carrot and coriander sambols, and a papadam to crumble in; mix everything Sri Lankan-style and add chilli or spice from the table (September–October 2026) · also pork, seafood and vegetarian curries, chicken vindaloo, small sizes (2026 reviews) · spiced tea; one October 2026 diner says the menu is supervised by a SriLankan Airlines group chef
